title.narrative: Catalyze Malawi: Sustainable Green Transition, Entrepreneurship Growth, and Alternative Finance Project

description.narrative: Malawi faces significant structural and economic challenges, rooted in its reliance on an undiversified, agro-based economy that accounts for approximately 30% of GDP and 80% of export earnings. This over-reliance exposes the country to vulnerabilities such as climate shocks, environmental degradation, and macroeconomic instability. Key barriers include limited investment in transformative sectors like trade, energy, and digital technology, compounded by logistical challenges due to its landlocked geography, high transportation costs, and inadequate infrastructure.A cascade of shocks, including the COVID-19 pandemic, geopolitical tensions, and local economic instability, has further undermined the country’s development gains and business environment.The Catalyze Malawi: Sustainable Green Transition, Entrepreneurship Growth, and Alternative Finance Project(2025–2028) aims to contribute in addressing such pressing issues by fostering sustainable economic growth andresilience through:1. Alternative Financing Mechanisms: Unlocking innovative financial solutions, such as green and blue bonds, to fund sustainable business growth and mobilize investments in Malawi’s green transition.2. Improved Business Environment: Strengthening the regulatory and operational framework to foster inclusive and green economic growth, reduce barriers to investment, and enable private sector competitiveness.3. Entrepreneurial Growth: Advancing startups and SMEs from idea stage to growth-oriented, export-ready enterprises, with an emphasis on women- and youth-led businesses.4. Green Transition: Supporting Malawi’s shift to a sustainable economy through investments in green businesses, clean energy solutions, and environmentally friendly practices.5. Agricultural Commercialization: Transitioning the agricultural sector into a commercially viable and market-oriented system, increasing productivity and value addition.By 2028, the project envisions a more resilient Malawian economy

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).
